Range

A slider for picking a number with the pointer.

HTML5 Range

Range is a styled input type="range". Dragging shows a bubble with the current value. It is not precise — pair it with a number field if the value must be exact.

Wrap the input in .range-field so the bubble can be positioned. min, max, step, and value are the native attributes. When they are omitted, the bubble treats the range as 0–100. 

<form action="#">
  <p class="range-field">
    <input type="range" id="test5" min="0" max="100" />
  </p>
</form>

Initialization

Range is not in AutoInit(). Importing the IIFE bundle calls RoutePlate.Range.Init() immediately, which starts every input[type=range] already in the document. Put the script after the inputs (as this site does), or call init yourself. no-autoinit does not apply. 

document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {
  const elems = document.querySelectorAll('input[type=range]');
  RoutePlate.Range.init(elems);
});

There are no options. For a range added after load:

RoutePlate.Range.init(document.querySelector('#test5'));

Methods

All methods are called on the plugin instance. You can get the instance like this: 
const instance = RoutePlate.Range.getInstance(elem);
.destroy();

Destroy the plugin instance, remove the value bubble, and tear down its event handlers.

instance.destroy();

Properties

Name Type Description
el Element The range input the plugin was initialized with.
options Object Empty. Range has no options.
thumb Element The generated bubble next to the input.
value Element The span inside the bubble that shows the current number.
